result.summary: This is a residential street characterized by row houses and embedded streetcar tracks in the roadway. While continuous sidewalks are provided on both sides, the environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings and traffic calming measures in the visible mid-block section.

hazards.name: Streetcar Tracks
hazards.description: Embedded metal tracks in the roadway create tripping hazards for pedestrians and slipping hazards for cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway running longitudinally

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and uneven surfaces around the streetcar tracks increase the risk of trips and falls.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross mid-block without protection.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at regular intervals to provide designated safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pavement Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair the degraded asphalt around the streetcar tracks to provide a smoother, safer surface for all users.

result.summary: The image shows a typical urban residential street with row houses and parallel on-street parking. While sidewalks are present on both sides, sightlines for pedestrians are significantly obstructed by parked vehicles and mature landscaping.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars and large bushes along the curb line block the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the left and right curbs throughout the block.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near the intersection to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and make pedestrians more visible.

result.summary: This residential street features embedded tram tracks and narrow sidewalks with no designated pedestrian crossings visible. The presence of on-street parking on both sides creates potential sightline obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Embedded Tram Tracks
hazards.description: Steel tracks in the roadway can be slippery when wet and present a tripping hazard or a risk for bicycle tires.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway extending into the distance

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street limits visibility between drivers and pedestrians wishing to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Crossings
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian infrastructure are visible along this stretch, forcing mid-block crossings without protection.

interventions.title: Marked Mid-block Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalk markings to designate safe crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install warning signs to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians in this residential area.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is severely compromised by active construction that has completely blocked the sidewalk with chain-link fencing. Pedestrians are forced to walk in the roadway without a protected temporary path, creating a high-risk situation. The presence of parked vehicles and construction equipment further limits visibility and available space for those navigating around the obstruction.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Blockage
hazards.description: Construction fencing completely blocks the sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into the travel lane of the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and center foreground, along the building frontage

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A parked white van and construction fencing obstruct sightlines between drivers and pedestrians walking in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, parked along the curb

interventions.title: Temporary Protected Walkway
interventions.description: Install a temporary pedestrian path using water-filled barriers or jersey barriers in the parking lane to provide a safe, separated space for walking around the construction site.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Closure Signage
interventions.description: Provide clear advance warning signs and detour information to direct pedestrians to the opposite sidewalk safely.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Parking Restrictions
interventions.description: Restrict parking immediately adjacent to the construction zone to improve visibility and create space for temporary pedestrian infrastructure.
